posts.text:
The Cato Institute is pleased to announce that constitutional attorney Molly Nixon is joining the Institute as Senior Fellow in Executive Power. 
cato.org/news-releases/molly…

Spain froze rents and capped increases at 2%, but rent control is already cutting supply by up to 50% and not improving conditions for renters. Spain should follow Argentina, which ended rent control in 2023 and has seen housing supply rise 180%, reports Cato’s @hiperfalcon. 
ow.ly/k7Mx50YztmZ

📚 Join Cato University in Phoenix on April 18 for a full day exploring liberty with leading scholars and peers. 

💫 Receive free resources and a $100 travel stipend upon completion. 

❗Space is limited. Apply before the deadline on April 8!

✅ Apply here: ow.ly/8JL750Yyenm

Congress should transfer TSA screening responsibilities to airports, allowing them to contract with specialized private security firms, writes Cato’s Chris Edwards. This would shield air travel from partisan gridlock in Washington while promoting efficiency and innovation.
cato.org/blog/fixing-airport…

Nothing like the Fairhaven Program existed in its community. Donald Antenen had to convince families not just that his microschool was good—but that this type of education was even possible. Cato's @ColleenHroncich profiles the founder who built it from scratch.  

cato.org/blog/friday-feature…

Trump wants to renew Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act “as is.” But the law needs fixing. Oversight is weak, it’s been abused, and courts have flagged constitutional issues. Reauthorizing it without changes could let surveillance run unchecked, warns Cato’s @PGEddington.
ow.ly/Tbp950Yztpl

Congress should not overlook the economic and fiscal consequences of a broken immigration system, Cato’s @David_J_Bier and @LettDominik said at a Capitol Hill briefing. They highlighted new research on immigrants’ effects on government budgets and outlined recommendations to improve DHS appropriations.

Kentucky’s “Blood Bill” touts medical freedom but mandates insurers and hospitals comply with directed-donation requests—raising costs, regulatory conflicts, and liability—while offering no real safety benefits. True autonomy thrives without government compulsion, says Cato’s @dr4liberty. 
ow.ly/s6P150YztnX

SNAP reform was supposed to cut improper payments—but there’s a loophole. States with the worst error rates can delay penalties, creating incentives to game the system instead of fixing it. Close the loopholes or expect more waste, say Cato’s @RominaBoccia and Tyler Turman. 

cato.org/blog/states-are-gam…

The US Surgeon General and the Public Health Service Commissioned Corps are relics of a bygone era - expensive, redundant, and counterproductive to modern public health. We need a decisive reform. Learn more from @dr4liberty.

Video
“This order and the case reflect serious questions of government power to punish a company for its speech and attempt to force it to change how it does business,” @jrhuddles explains.

A preliminary injunction in the Anthropic case means that the underlying issues extend beyond just a dispute over procurement policy or the appropriate redlines for government use of AI technology, says the Cato Institute’s @jrhuddles.

President Trump’s approach to war: strike first, think later. From Iran to Venezuela, his military actions lack clear objectives, turning tactical wins into endless conflict and repeating the very “forever war” problem he once condemned, says Cato’s @brandan_buck. ow.ly/JQ2P50Yztkq

All immigrants, both legal and illegal, are less likely to be incarcerated than native-born Americans, the 2010-2024 data show. 

Check out the new study by @AlexNowrasteh and Michelangelo Landgrove, “Illegal Immigrant Incarceration Rates, 2010–2024: The Demographics of American Imprisonment.” 

ow.ly/YN1Z50YyQLs

When government restricts who can practice medicine and how, patients pay the price. And considering the US faces a looming doctor shortage, lawmakers should grow the pool of health care providers ready to care for patients.

cato.org/blog/restricting-cl…

Why are economists nearly unanimous in opposing rent control? 

Because it shrinks rental supply, degrades housing quality, and tends to benefit longer-term, higher-income tenants rather than the low-income renters it claims to help.  
Listen to the new Cato Podcast episode with @MrRBourne and @jeffreyamiron. 

Apple: ow.ly/oBBk50YzqKF  
Spotify: ow.ly/4iWl50YzqKC  
Website: ow.ly/V46550YzqKE

Body cams, visible identification, not knowingly detaining and deporting US citizens—none of it matters if there’s no accountability. Without the ability to hold federal agents personally liable, “reform” is just a pinky promise, says Cato’s @foxmike90. 

ow.ly/XYHE50YyJRY
